newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia warns against communist spectre.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia warns against communist spectre.

text.p: Indonesian President Suharto on Tuesday led a ceremony at the monument for generals killed in an abortive 1965 coup bid, as the government warned the country's 196 million people of the dangers of communism.
The now banned Indonesian Communist Party (PKI) has been blamed for the coup attempt, after which at least 500,000 people are estimated to have died in an anti-communist purge.

The government's crusade against communism normally peaks at the end of September, but some political analysts said it was using the anniversary this year to justify a crackdown on dissent after the July 27 riots that rocked Jakarta.

It has accused the small, leftist People's Democratic Party (PRD) for the riots and has made clear that it will not tolerate dissident political activity ahead of general elections due in May next year.

At Tuesday's ceremony at the Pancasila Sanctity Monument in East Jakarta, Armed Forces chief General Fiesal Tanjung said the annual ritual was intended to remind the younger generation of the "cruelty of communism" and its threat to Indonesian society.
"We have already seen the proof with the PRD recently," Tanjung told reporters.

Suharto, in 1965 a major-general heading the elite strategic reserve, was one of the few senior officers to survive the coup. Six generals were killed and their bodies thrown into a well known as the crocodile hole where the monument now stands.

In March 1966, Suharto took executive control from founding President Sukarno, who was accused of having links to the coup plotters. Suharto formally became president in 1968 and has since held the post unopposed for six five-year terms.

Political analysts say the government engineered the ousting of Sukarno's daughter, Megawati Sukarnoputri, as leader of the minority Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) last June, fearing that she would draw votes from the ruling Golkar next year.

The July 27 riots followed a police raid to evict her supporters from the official PDI headquarters. The PDI, Golkar and the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) are the only three groups legally permitted to contest elections.
Official warnings against the threat of "latent" communism reach an annual crescendo with television broadcasts of a film dramatisation of the coup and the commemoration ceremony.
"The Pancasila Sanctity Day...should be used as momentum for the nation to keep its vigil against the latent danger of communism," Information Minister Harmoko said on Monday.
In his prayer at Tuesday's ceremony, Religious Affairs Minister Tarmizi Taher thanked God for saving the nation from the communist threat, including what he said were its remnants like the PRD.
"It's just adding another chapter to the a familiar theme. It's not unusual in intensity but it adds to the myths that sustain the regime," a Western diplomat said.
"By associating something with the PKI, they are not necessarily saying this is communist but are sending a message that these are not legitimate political activities," he said.
The PRD, in a statement received by fax on Tuesday, rejected the government's claims that it was communist and said Indonesia's youth knew communism was dead.
"The PRD was founded by young people who in their own time have seen the symbols of communism collapse, including the fall of the Berlin Wall...," the statement said.
